data.title: Cap Low-priority requests per batch

criteria.given: a cap of 2 and a batch of 5 LOW requests with distinct requestedAt plus 3 non-LOW requests, all passing validation and deduplication
criteria.then: the accepted queue holds the 2 LOW requests with the earliest requestedAt plus all 3 non-LOW requests, and the other 3 LOW requests are reported as problems with code ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP (never silently dropped); only Priority.LOW counts against the cap

criteria.given: a cap of 1 and LOW requests 'B-2' and 'A-1' both at 2026-10-20T08:00:00Z
criteria.then: 'A-1' is kept and 'B-2' is reported over cap: ties on requestedAt break by requestId ascending, the same ordering the sorter already uses

criteria.given: any batch containing more LOW requests than the cap
criteria.when: the same batch is shuffled and processed 100 times
criteria.then: the accepted queue, the set of over-cap requestIds and the trace are identical every time

criteria.given: a cap of 0
criteria.when: a batch of 2 LOW and 1 HIGH request is processed
criteria.then: only the HIGH request is accepted and both LOW requests get OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP problems; a cap of 0 is legal and means no Low work is accepted

criteria.given: a cap of 0 and two duplicates whose group's highest priority is MEDIUM, so the kept request is escalated from LOW to MEDIUM
criteria.then: the kept request is accepted with no cap problem: the cap uses the priority as it stands after the deduplicate stage

criteria.given: a LOW request 'WR-9' at input index 4 over a cap of 2
criteria.then: the Problem has inputIndex 4, requestId 'WR-9', code OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP, null field, relatedRequestId, escalatedFrom and escalatedTo, and message exactly "WR-9 exceeds the per-batch Low-priority cap of 2"; OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP is appended last in ProblemCode and BatchObserver still increments one counter per ProblemCode value

criteria.given: a cap of 1, a batch that also yields validation and duplicate problems, and over-cap LOW requests 'L-2' at input index 7 and 'L-3' at input index 3
criteria.then: cap problems appear in the prioritize stage, after validate and deduplicate problems and ordered by input index (index 3 before index 7); the prioritize StageTrace has stage "prioritize", out == in - 2, and notes exactly ["L-2 dropped: over Low-priority cap of 1", "L-3 dropped: over Low-priority cap of 1"] sorted naturally with no input indices

criteria.given: a batch with no LOW request over the cap, an empty batch, or a null batch
criteria.then: no OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP problem is produced, the prioritize trace has in == out and no cap note, and the trace still has exactly three entries: validate, deduplicate, prioritize

criteria.given: an application context with no app.batch.max-low-priority configured
criteria.then: maxLowPriority() is 1000 (@DefaultValue("1000") on the new second component) and maxSize() is still 5000, and ProcessingConfig builds the WorkRequestSorter bean with BatchProperties.maxLowPriority()

criteria.given: app.batch.max-low-priority = -1
criteria.then: IllegalArgumentException is thrown with message "app.batch.max-low-priority must be at least 0, was -1"; 0 and positive values are accepted

criteria.given: existing callers of new BatchProperties(5000), new WorkRequestSorter(), new WorkRequestProcessor(validator, resolver, sorter) and the 13-request sample batch
criteria.when: they are compiled and run after the change
criteria.then: they still compile and behave as before: BatchProperties(int maxSize) delegates to maxLowPriority 1000, the no-arg WorkRequestSorter() applies no cap, capping is reached only via new WorkRequestSorter(int maxLowPriority), and the sample batch still gives the same queue, problems and counts 13 → 10 → 6

outOfScope: Caps for MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL priorities
Per-sender or per-equipment quotas rather than a per-batch cap
Changing the existing sort order or deduplication rules
Exposing the cap or remaining Low capacity in the API response DTOs
Rejecting a whole batch when the cap is exceeded
Introducing a Clock bean or any time-based staleness logic
